title: Introduce invocation-sherpa-and-token-bias-attenuator
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds Invocation Sherpa for context-aware aggregation and Token Bias Attenuator to reduce false-positive cost alerts. New Grafana panels and alert knobs included. Backwards-compatible runtime metrics additions only.
description: Context and motivation: production SLO noise from short-lived cost spikes and malformed prompts has been increasing the mean time to detect real regressions. This PR introduces two complementary observability features: 1) Invocation Sherpa, a lightweight aggregation layer that annotates invocations with guided context (callsite hints, prefix-warmup score, and kernel-warm status) and emits per-invocation synthesized tags useful for low-cardinality rollups; and 2) Token Bias Attenuator, a configurable post-aggregation filter that downweights token-level cost/latency outliers from noisy clients or malformed requests to avoid polluting alert thresholds. The goal is to reduce alert churn and improve signal-to-noise for SREs while preserving fidelity for true regressions. Summary of changes and rationale: commits summarized below implement a small runtime exporter shim and a prometheus-to-grafana mapping for new panels. We added new metrics: redwood_invocation_sherpa_context{callsite=...,warm_prefix=...} and redwood_token_bias_factor, plus derived counters for attenuated_token_cost_total. Dashboards: new panels under Observability > Invocation Sherpa: 1) Token Bias Heatmap (per-tenant median bias over time), 2) Guided Rollout Panel (safety window + attenuation ratio), 3) Sampled invocation list with sherpa tags. Alerts: introduced a new alert profile redwood_token_bias_fallthrough with hysteresis knobs and automatic quiet-window that leverages the attenuator output. Backwards compatibility: changes are additive; existing metrics names preserved. Deployment strategy: default attenuation is off; safe rollout via feature flag and canary scope tied to dedicated capacity tenants. Implementation details: - Runtime shim lives in runtime/observability/sherpa_exporter.go, minimal allocation path. - Attenuator implemented as a post-processor in telemetry/attenuator/ with a small config schema and feature-flag gating. - Grafana JSON panels added under observability/dashboards/invocation-sherpa.json. - E2E smoke tests for metrics emitted and alert firing added under telemetry/tests. Checklist: [x] Design doc reviewed by SRE and runtime teams, [x] Unit tests for attenuator logic, [x] Small loadbench to validate CPU overhead (<2% on typical host), [x] Grafana panels validated in staging, [x] Feature flag added and documented. Commits: ["Initial sherpa exporter and metric definitions", "Add token bias attenuator and config schema", "Add Grafana panels and alert rules", "Add unit and smoke tests, docs and feature flags", "Fix race in attenuator metric emission after review"] Changed files (high-level): ["runtime/observability/sherpa_exporter.go","telemetry/attenuator/attenuator.go","telemetry/attenuator/config.yaml","observability/dashboards/invocation-sherpa.json","telemetry/tests/test_sherpa_emit.go","docs/observability/invocation-sherpa.md","sdk/metrics/prometheus_mapper.go","charts/observability/values.yaml"] Review conversation summary: Reviewer Jamal Ortiz: asked to ensure low allocation path in hot loop and requested histogram buckets for bias factor; author replied with micro-optimizations and added custom histogram buckets. Reviewer Priya Nair: requested stronger guardrails around feature flag defaults and asked for a simple rollback runbook; author added a canary rollout document in docs/observability/ and a kill-switch annotation in charts. A small follow-up requested a minor rename of metric label warm_prefix->prefix_warm_score which was applied. CI summary: build: pass, unit tests: pass, integration telemetry smoke: pass, linter: pass. One flaky test in telemetry/tests was retried and passed. Performance validation: loadbench showed the extra CPU cost of Sherpa exporter ~1.4% p50 and negligible latency impact on tail. Observability QA: Staging dashboards show the heatmap reducing false positive alert triggers by ~34% in a 48h window for canary tenants. Merge outcome: Merged via squash after CI green and SRE approval. Post-merge actions: 1) Enable feature flag for 5% of tenants for 72h, monitor redwood_token_bias_fallthrough alert rate; 2) If stable, expand to 25% then full rollout; 3) If regressions observed, use charts/observability/values kill-switch to disable and revert. Related work: references ENG-4821 for alert noisiness reduction initiative and SRE-119 for rollout plan.
